title: Initial acceleration magnitude
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly compute the initial acceleration as 6.4 m/s², accounting for both gravity and the initial electrostatic repulsion.

title: Maximum speed condition
description: Important Criteria: The student must recognize that the speed is maximum when the net force on charge B is zero (i.e., when electrostatic force equals gravitational force).

title: Distance L calculation
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly solve the force-balance equation to find the distance L = 0.3 m.

title: Force direction analysis
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly identify that both forces are vertical and that the electrostatic force is upward (repulsive) while gravity is downward.

title: Correct force expressions
description: Important Criteria: The student must properly write the expressions for gravitational force (mg) and Coulomb force (kqQ/r²) with correct charge magnitudes.

title: Sign error in forces
description: Pitfall Criteria: Deduct points if the student incorrectly adds the forces (treating them as both in the same direction) instead of subtracting them.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional Criteria: The student may show unit analysis to verify that the computed acceleration has units of m/s² and distance has units of meters.

title: Energy method alternative
description: Optional Criteria: The student may use energy conservation (potential energy minimum) as an alternative approach to find the maximum speed position.
